Tannins are naturally occurring polyphenol compounds found in grape skins, seeds, stems, and oak barrels that add structure, bitterness, and an astringent, drying texture to wine.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_B8tVCnIFVbzPeh_4HNFcIlX8HSxgB4k0xYfT8av_PvdnDPK0g7N9-k6kTXQSNs78iAt3EPfQBZA35eKtmtYWO7MaJCckPdPhHXa8D_XUDYAIC1QvwlYauQzXqwAXehR6PTsP-Uy6d1X7xk85DIMNtUy4xBkktMXFhTYrQtho0)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXQYEgk0wEfjAPZg07Ii6zrcjAbSkp-YkKgxmHsPSXV4cStKDDTzCwvlIubFQbnv8yvkQ9GW-FuDHjcmMJOQUQREcvuxvGyDlmQ686RtsGB8mrkDqC3b0YXT7gtBOIbPLTsxTbKdw)

### What They Taste and Feel Like

- **Astringency vs. bitterness:** Tannins create a drying, puckering, or "sandpapery" sensation on your gums, tongue, and cheeks—similar to oversteeped black tea or walnut skins—alongside subtle bitterness.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXQYEgk0wEfjAPZg07Ii6zrcjAbSkp-YkKgxmHsPSXV4cStKDDTzCwvlIubFQbnv8yvkQ9GW-FuDHjcmMJOQUQREcvuxvGyDlmQ686RtsGB8mrkDqC3b0YXT7gtBOIbPLTsxTbKdw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXZ3jRGjsJzZPQOTc0aBTLz55sacV6kjEMfl-8vAQq9bkmfAo7T1cK3EsIE61leVmvxCrRSHD3rjdbFpQADZojiQvcdvsiEQd2i-3Ino7BL5SQTdKvJT8-qCxn7dbql3ur)
- **How they affect your body:** Tannins bind to proteins (including lubricating proteins in your saliva), reducing moisture in your mouth. They also act as antioxidants and natural preservatives.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXLklE5mEQnXSCyyxujh-ULWWqj2n00dfbBxc1ojEJd8S-nkAIBzZZYC1hOkkdvmx2FW8smld9vDSG8kuB8exZ6gNpjAEgR5J9Ul-FAJOpQclQmdlk6BhvpTUA-9maiJjaQaAcFzFV)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_B8tVCnIFVbzPeh_4HNFcIlX8HSxgB4k0xYfT8av_PvdnDPK0g7N9-k6kTXQSNs78iAt3EPfQBZA35eKtmtYWO7MaJCckPdPhHXa8D_XUDYAIC1QvwlYauQzXqwAXehR6PTsP-Uy6d1X7xk85DIMNtUy4xBkktMXFhTYrQtho0)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXtJBZ3bcw4iR6e1IFxM1YyySlUdiNUp8SWScA6RzcsjVt8xMVkLZ330MKNQhYhe8ccdNH8h8tLClNMI7uNlIdSzkKZwyAkYawvuwxlDstajGEtA1OAPfLw57EjJEZ3YmL)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)

### Tannin Levels Across Wines

- **High-tannin reds:** Tannat, Sagrantino, Nebbiolo, Cabernet Sauvignon, Petite Sirah, Petit Verdot, and Syrah/Shiraz.
- **Low- to medium-tannin reds:** Pinot Noir, Gamay, Merlot, and Grenache.
- **White, rosé, and sparkling wines:** Typically very low in tannins because they have little to no skin contact during fermentation (orange wine is a notable exception).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF10Ww7Fi1hqa9HR0-pqx51gZx4FXtvvTwSw2knuSbdufHE21oCQHakKLdPpiumCi9LBpsuHTqUrwKYbC8HfijF8HJk1bXFk60TTT_xOKo0oDmcwgAFmwAwHAWrNEQGEB28Xr2fkY1q1vF7LhcVosPyu5bDzbruDKi9Lf9ew)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESagHEIkXXQYEgk0wEfjAPZg07Ii6zrcjAbSkp-YkKgxmHsPSXV4cStKDDTzCwvlIubFQbnv8yvkQ9GW-FuDHjcmMJOQUQREcvuxvGyDlmQ686RtsGB8mrkDqC3b0YXT7gtBOIbPLTsxTbKdw)[[5]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZQHEIkXXtJBZ3bcw4iR6e1IFxM1YyySlUdiNUp8SWScA6RzcsjVt8xMVkLZ330MKNQhYhe8ccdNH8h8tLClNMI7uNlIdSzkKZwyAkYawvuwxlDstajGEtA1OAPfLw57EjJEZ3YmL)

### Aging and Softening Tannins

- **Aging:** Tannins act as a structural backbone and antioxidant. Over years in the bottle, tannin molecules link together and bind with pigment compounds, gradually softening into a smoother texture and sometimes forming natural sediment.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXRDACHw56qQLIHZ7yvIlNqOmV17E4UU8OTK7Mie1uxiq9RsUQ55SeWEQSMkzMt_Sr46TBA7DLjckvjXh9iAhghZRxMZuHgQYiJQmowoU7BQ3UoWX8aQ4jdNoKTVH1iHIQ5wKtJAda2g)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_B8tVCnIFVbzPeh_4HNFcIlX8HSxgB4k0xYfT8av_PvdnDPK0g7N9-k6kTXQSNs78iAt3EPfQBZA35eKtmtYWO7MaJCckPdPhHXa8D_XUDYAIC1QvwlYauQzXqwAXehR6PTsP-Uy6d1X7xk85DIMNtUy4xBkktMXFhTYrQtho0)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESawHEIkXXLklE5mEQnXSCyyxujh-ULWWqj2n00dfbBxc1ojEJd8S-nkAIBzZZYC1hOkkdvmx2FW8smld9vDSG8kuB8exZ6gNpjAEgR5J9Ul-FAJOpQclQmdlk6BhvpTUA-9maiJjaQaAcFzFV)
- **Food pairings:** Rich, protein-heavy, and fatty foods (such as marbled steak or aged cheeses) bind with tannins and cut through fat, making bold wines feel smoother. For a deeper dive into tannin types and tasting notes, see [Wine Folly](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9) or [Lake Chelan Wine Valley](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_B8tVCnIFVbzPeh_4HNFcIlX8HSxgB4k0xYfT8av_PvdnDPK0g7N9-k6kTXQSNs78iAt3EPfQBZA35eKtmtYWO7MaJCckPdPhHXa8D_XUDYAIC1QvwlYauQzXqwAXehR6PTsP-Uy6d1X7xk85DIMNtUy4xBkktMXFhTYrQtho0)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF10Ww7Fi1hqa9HR0-pqx51gZx4FXtvvTwSw2knuSbdufHE21oCQHakKLdPpiumCi9LBpsuHTqUrwKYbC8HfijF8HJk1bXFk60TTT_xOKo0oDmcwgAFmwAwHAWrNEQGEB28Xr2fkY1q1vF7LhcVosPyu5bDzbruDKi9Lf9ew)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)

For a deeper dive into tannin types and tasting notes, see [Wine Folly](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9) or [Lake Chelan Wine Valley](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShAEBxCJF1_B8tVCnIFVbzPeh_4HNFcIlX8HSxgB4k0xYfT8av_PvdnDPK0g7N9-k6kTXQSNs78iAt3EPfQBZA35eKtmtYWO7MaJCckPdPhHXa8D_XUDYAIC1QvwlYauQzXqwAXehR6PTsP-Uy6d1X7xk85DIMNtUy4xBkktMXFhTYrQtho0)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF1zS2shgkUdhypJ4CfcxxUU4F2XFDbBKpHwGFLcUOR6RXf1AmsDvVsSab2NIMozE9r3qrEDCDBYLihalK-JQiVEpknpCHnZJCtqGUmat06X27V_BcBqXm__2pOw4p_LmpQfTVaalrWddaIpK536iq_ZH6KmXs-JECfiU98bXPZQigUEucny2lzic5nOaNUg)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESgAEBxCJF10Ww7Fi1hqa9HR0-pqx51gZx4FXtvvTwSw2knuSbdufHE21oCQHakKLdPpiumCi9LBpsuHTqUrwKYbC8HfijF8HJk1bXFk60TTT_xOKo0oDmcwgAFmwAwHAWrNEQGEB28Xr2fkY1q1vF7LhcVosPyu5bDzbruDKi9Lf9ew)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScQHEIkXXIbVEDsUGb6J7lGXvcDvDxXKVrUc7fxrzIpt-85TYxUTV4ozlpnHdXqH5USgvO_g1cutBfDra79RPKJj1bnG38rQLEBpfOGYaKI8041If_CE0dB4-PYphkEvxc9PKXtznLG23mZYGt117ZVu9)

expanded_element.title: Tannins and human health: a review - PubMed
expanded_element.snippet: Tannins have also been reported to exert other physiological effects, such as to accelerate blood clotting, reduce blood pressure, decrease the serum lipid level, produce liver necrosis, and modulate immunoresponses. The dosage and kind of tannins are critical to these effects.

expanded_element.title: Tannins in Wine: Taste, Mouthfeel, and Quality Explained
expanded_element.snippet: Essentially, tannins add bitterness and astringency. These two qualities are evident when you're drinking a young wine, making it feel harsh on your tongue and drying out your mouth. The taste can be shockingly, mouth-puckeringly astringent, or “green.”
